Question B-003-015-001.

Why the correct answer is right: Voice, images, and other analog information can be sampled or encoded into digital data before transmission.

Per-choice notes:
- sourceIndex 0: "Any analog information can be converted to digital data": This is the correct choice because voice, images, and other analog information can be sampled or encoded into digital data before transmission.
- sourceIndex 1: "Digital protocols can fall back to analog as needed": This is a near-miss because it shifts attention from Any analog information can be converted to digital data. In digital information, packet forwarding, weak-signal modes, and sound-card drive level, analog conversion is a different idea from the digital-data function being tested.
- sourceIndex 2: "Digital signals are continuously variable signals": This answer would fit a different fault than Any analog information can be converted to digital data. In digital information, packet forwarding, weak-signal modes, and sound-card drive level, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
- sourceIndex 3: "Modern transceivers have the necessary high efficiency amplifiers": This option confuses another station topic with Any analog information can be converted to digital data. In digital information, packet forwarding, weak-signal modes, and sound-card drive level, it names a different cause, control, component, or safety action than the one required here.
